newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast lt. crudes higher in light trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast lt. crudes higher in light trade.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crude prices edged up Friday, influenced by higher gasoline markets on the New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX), traders said.
In local spot markets, no cargoes traded of Alaska North Slope (ANS) traded Friday, but BP Oil, its main producer, offered at $1.85 under September West Texas Intermediate/Cushing (WTI).
Earlier this week, ANS sold to a small refinery at a $2.08 discount, slightly tighter than the $2.16 discount sold in June.
Bids were heard at $2.08 under, traders said.
Kern River and Wilmington grades rose after all major oil companies raised their postings last night.
A posting plus deal on Kern River was heard at 40 cent a barrel mid-week, but no party confirmed the deal.
